transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been having a little trouble at the lab lately. I'm a physical scientist, and usually I'm very on top of things, but... I just can't seem to keep my mind on the actual experiment anymore. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. 

Like, I'll be in the middle of an important grant call, or a safety meeting, and I'll just... I'll notice a pump vibrating, or hear a student's side comment, or even just picture some odd peak in an old spectrum. And then, before I know it, suddenly I'm off chasing that one little thing for hours. Meanwhile, the main work, the thing everyone actually needs from me, just kind of falls apart. I feel terrible about letting my team down, I really do. 

I hope that's the kind of thing you can help with... am I explaining that okay?
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or unusually up for several days?

Um... well, energized, yes. I guess for the last few months, I've actually felt really... good? Like, almost electrified, honestly. It just felt like the lab was finally moving at my speed for once. I thought I was just being a really proactive leader, you know? 

But... um... I guess I should be completely honest. I'm a little ashamed to admit this, but... if someone questions my plan, or asks me to slow down, I've... well, I've been snapping at them. Which really isn't like me! I try so hard to be a supportive mentor. But I've been so sharp with them lately that... well, I've noticed some of the students are actually starting to avoid my office entirely. 

I feel just terrible about it. I really don't want to be a difficult person to work with, and I hate that I've made them uncomfortable... does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking...
During this period of feeling electrified, have you been needing less sleep than usual?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I have been sleeping a bit less. But honestly, it hasn't felt like a bad thing! I hope you don't think I'm being irresponsible with my health, but... it's just been so nice to have extra time in the day. 

Lately, most nights I probably only get about two or three hours of sleep. Sometimes I don't even make it to bed, I just sort of doze off on the couch with my laptop still open. But the funny thing is, I don't wake up feeling exhausted or groggy at all. I wake up feeling incredibly sharp, just completely ready to dive right back into my work. It almost feels like... well, like sleeping a full eight hours would just be an inefficient interruption right now, with how much I'm getting done. 

I know that probably sounds a little strange... is it okay that I'm functioning well on that amount of sleep? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During this energized period, have you felt more capable or important than usual?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I don't want to sound arrogant, I really don't, because I value my colleagues so much. But... I suppose recently I have felt... very capable. 

I mean, we have this massive multi-site project going on, and things were getting so bogged down. And I just... I genuinely believed I could fix all of it by myself. I was absolutely certain I could redesign our entire spectroscopy approach overnight, and... well, I kind of thought I could mentor every single student on the project better than their actual advisors were doing. I figured I could just take on all their work and still easily beat the big grant deadline. 

I just felt so sure that if everyone would just step back and stop getting in my way, I could save the whole project single-handedly. I know that sounds terribly conceited when I say it out loud... I really try to be a team player, I promise. Do you think it's normal to get a little overconfident when you're feeling that energetic? I hope I don't sound too awful admitting that...
During this energized period, has your behavior caused serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Um... well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... yes. There have been some... complications. 

I really hate to admit this, because I take my job so seriously, but... the department head actually had to step in recently. I thought I was juggling everything perfectly, but I guess I missed some key priorities, and... well, my scheduling got a bit confused. With me trying to take over everyone's mentoring, the supervision structure got really strained. 

They... um... they told me I was putting the project at risk. And even worse, they said I was compromising lab safety expectations, just because I was moving so fast and trying to do too much at once. They've actually taken away some of the decision-making I used to handle. 

I feel so embarrassed even saying it out loud. I promise I never meant to cause any trouble or put anyone at risk. I just got so caught up in trying to help... I hope you don't think I'm a negligent scientist. I really do care about my lab and my students. Is it... is it common for things to get a little out of hand like that when you're feeling so sped up?
